name: Chandranshu Sinha
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, EkAnek Networks (Foxy beauty-shopping app); co-founder of OfBusiness
profile: Indian technologist who co-founded B2B commerce and lending unicorn OfBusiness (OFB Tech), where he headed products. In 2018 he co-founded EkAnek Networks, which runs Foxy, an artist-led online shopping platform for beauty, grooming and personal care, where he serves as CTO.
interesting_fact: After helping build OfBusiness, he left to co-found Foxy (EkAnek Networks, founded 2018) alongside Kartik Sheth, Nikhil Gilani and Sachin Singhal.
notes: No longer listed on OfBusiness's current team page (https://www.ofbusiness.com/about/team?tab=team); best route is via Foxy/EkAnek. Background reportedly IIT Kharagpur, DevFactory and Trilogy, but that comes from a single weak source (CrazyEngineers), so it is not used as a fact. Low public profile.

name: Grant LaFontaine
profile: Maine-raised consumer-tech product executive who co-founded Whatnot with Logan Head in 2019. It went through Y Combinator's Winter 2020 batch, starting with Funko Pops before expanding into trading cards, fashion and more. Whatnot is now a leading US live-stream shopping platform, reported by Fortune at a $20B valuation in 2026.
interesting_fact: While raising money, the founders pitched hundreds of investors and logged each rejection in a spreadsheet, but stopped updating it at 100 rows because they were too 'demoralized'. Whatnot's first livestream, which LaFontaine hosted, sold out in about 2.5 hours.
deep_cut_fact: He opened an eBay store in fourth grade, selling Pokemon cards with friends in Maine. His first online sale was a holographic Chansey card, the sale that hooked him as both a collector and a seller.
notes: Could not verify a current Whatnot press email in this session. 2022 Business Wire releases reportedly listed Moxie PR (whatnot@moxiegrouppr.com) as the agency, but I could not open those pages to confirm, so it is not listed as a contact. Has appeared on the a16z and Masters of Scale podcasts.

name: Chaitanya Kanojia
current_role: Co-founder of Starry (fixed-wireless broadband); stepped down as CEO in June 2023 and was reported to stay on the board
profile: Chaitanya 'Chet' Kanojia is a Boston-area serial telecom/media entrepreneur. He ran Navic Networks, an advanced TV advertising firm Microsoft acquired in 2008. He then founded Aereo, a cloud-antenna TV service, followed by Starry, a fixed-wireless home internet provider founded around 2014 that listed via SPAC in 2022. He handed Starry's CEO role to COO Alex Moulle-Berteaux in June 2023.
interesting_fact: His earlier startup Aereo, which put an over-the-air TV antenna and DVR in the cloud, took its fight with broadcasters all the way to the US Supreme Court. He then built Starry as his next attempt to disrupt incumbent networks.
deep_cut_fact: Some of his investors at FirstMark have known him for about 20 years. He told TechCrunch he wanted backers who had 'seen that movie', meaning stayed with a company from seed stage all the way to IPO.
notes: Starry went through Chapter 11 in 2023 and was taken private; avoid this topic in outreach. In the 2023 transition post he said he wanted to dedicate more time to his family. His current activity is unclear. Highly relevant to a telecom/infrastructure podcast.

name: Grzegorz Kokosiński
current_role: Listed in the Founders section of Starburst's leadership page as Senior Manager, Engineering; Trino open-source maintainer
profile: Polish software engineer in the Warsaw-based founding engineering team of Starburst, the commercial company behind the Trino (formerly PrestoSQL) distributed SQL query engine. The team grew out of Hadapt/Teradata's Presto work. Starburst lists him among its founders as Senior Manager, Engineering.
interesting_fact: Starburst's own leadership page groups him with co-founders Kamil Bajda-Pawlikowski, Matt Fuller and Piotr Findeisen in its 'Founders' section, part of the Warsaw engineering team behind Starburst.
deep_cut_fact: He is one of the official maintainers of the open-source Trino SQL engine, listed under the GitHub handle 'kokosing' on Trino's project roles page.
notes: Low-profile engineer, not an executive. One search summary claimed his LinkedIn says his Starburst role was eliminated; this was not verified, and Starburst's leadership page still lists him. Starburst has no press email on its leadership page, only a general /contact/ form. The LinkedIn URL comes from search results and was not opened.

name: Rajesh Yabaji
current_role: Chairman, Managing Director & CEO, BlackBuck Ltd (formerly Zinka Logistics Solutions; listed on NSE/BSE)
profile: IIT Kharagpur alumnus and former ITC supply-chain manager who co-founded BlackBuck in 2015 with ITC colleague Chanakya Hridaya and Ramasubramaniam B. The company began as a B2B full-truckload freight marketplace and grew into India's largest digital platform for truck operators, covering FASTag/fuel payments, telematics, loads and vehicle financing. It is now a listed company with Yabaji as chairman, MD and CEO.
interesting_fact: BlackBuck's growth exploded after India mandated FASTags for toll payments in 2019. Yabaji told Fortune India that '99% of the growth in business happened after 2019.'
deep_cut_fact: The idea came from his ITC project to modernise a 100-year-old supply chain. He could improve planning and warehousing, but transportation stayed out of reach because it was in the hands of fragmented truck owners.
notes: The deep-cut fact is from a search summary of the 2016 YourStory piece, which I did not open directly. Its ITC origin story matches Fortune India's account. BlackBuck runs regular investor calls, so the IR route is the most reliable.

name: Paul Sawaya
current_role: Founder & CEO, Elsewhere (multiplayer roguelike game startup, SF); co-founder and former CTO of Human Interest
profile: San Francisco engineer who co-founded Human Interest in 2015 with Roger Lee. The YC S15 digital 401(k) provider automated retirement plans for small businesses, and Sawaya was its founding CTO for about five years and sat on its board. He is now an angel investor and founder/CEO of Elsewhere, an a16z Speedrun gaming/AI-agents startup.
interesting_fact: After Human Interest, he switched to games: his new company Elsewhere pitches itself as 'the multiplayer roguelike of your dreams' and is backed through a16z's Speedrun program.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Human Interest he built a Facebook app, worked at Bloomberg, and interviewed with Emmett Shear at Justin.tv. He spent about two years 'wandering in the wilderness' exploring ideas before settling on small-business 401(k)s.
notes: No longer operational at Human Interest. Best route is X (@automin) or LinkedIn. Interested in WebAssembly and AI-driven interfaces.

name: Mario Ciabarra
current_role: Founder & CEO, Quantum Metric (digital analytics, Colorado)
profile: Penn State-educated serial founder and son of an immigrant family, the youngest of six, from Montgomery County, PA. He sold his app-performance-monitoring startup DevStream to Compuware, built iPhone app businesses Intelliborn and Rock Your Phone, and in 2015 co-founded Quantum Metric with hacker David Wang. Quantum Metric became Colorado's first tech unicorn after a $200M Insight-led round in 2021.
interesting_fact: Quantum Metric passed $100M in annual recurring revenue in December 2022 and says it captures insights from about 45% of the world's internet users. Penn State's podcast called him the first unicorn founder to start a business in Colorado.
deep_cut_fact: At Penn State he started YourNotes.com, which paid students to take class notes and published them free for other students, funded by sponsors, as a challenge to paid service Nittany Notes. He says he still hates taking notes.
notes: As a teen he resold arcade tokens and sold candy and donuts (Insight Partners profile: https://www.insightpartners.com/ideas/how-mario-ciabarra-is-reimagining-customer-experiences-for-the-fortune-100-with-quantum-metric/). He was a guest on Penn State's 'Dare to Disrupt' podcast.

name: Zhang Buzheng
current_role: Executive Director, Chairman & CEO, YSB Inc. (Yaoshibang / 药师帮, HKEX: 9885)
profile: Zhang Buzhen (张步镇) is the founder of Guangzhou-based Yaoshibang (YSB), a B2B pharmaceutical e-commerce and services platform connecting drug makers and distributors with China's pharmacies and clinics. He founded it in January 2015 after about 15 years at SouFun/Fang Holdings. YSB listed in Hong Kong on 28 June 2023.
interesting_fact: Before healthcare, he spent about 15 years at SouFun (Fang.com), China's property portal, growing with the company to become its CTO and then the VP running its website, technology, product and mobile operations.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a 1997 bachelor's degree in communications engineering from the Beijing Electronic Science and Technology Institute (北京电子科技学院). He joined SouFun in April 1999, when it was still an early-stage internet startup.
notes: The input spells his name 'Zhang Buzheng'; filings use Zhang Buzhen / 张步镇. The education and SouFun dates come from a search summary of a Lixinger executive resume, which I could not open directly. No dedicated IR email found; best route is HKEX filings or the company's IR channel. Chinese-language outreach is advisable.

name: Pierre Louis Lacoste
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Brand Officer, Ankorstore (Paris B2B wholesale marketplace); current title per MarketScreener, not confirmed on Ankorstore's own site
profile: French e-commerce entrepreneur who co-founded Ankorstore in 2019 with Nicolas d'Audiffret, Nicolas Cohen and Mathieu Alengrin. Ankorstore is a wholesale marketplace connecting independent brands with independent shops across Europe. Before that he was a VP at activewear brand Lolë and Etsy's Country Manager for France. Ankorstore raised a €250M Series C in 2022 at unicorn valuation.
interesting_fact: Ankorstore is partly a second attempt at an idea Etsy dropped: at Etsy he worked on Etsy Wholesale, which was cancelled when Etsy refocused on consumers. 'I always thought it was a missed opportunity, but also that I would do a few things differently.'
deep_cut_fact: Before building a platform for independent retailers he ran one himself: he owned a multi-brand retail store for several years, and says this taught him how hard it is for shops to find brands and agree terms.
notes: Nicolas d'Audiffret, not Lacoste, is Ankorstore's CEO. The PR agency contact is from a March 2024 release and may be dated. No recent (2025-26) coverage of Lacoste found.

name: Xi Gang
current_role: Chairman, New Hope Dairy (新乳业, SZSE 002946); President of Caogen Zhiben (草根知本); Chairman of Xianshenghuo cold chain (Fresh-SCM)
profile: Xi Gang (席刚) is a New Hope Group veteran of 25+ years who has led New Hope Dairy since joining it in 2004. He built it through acquisitions into a 'fleet' of regional fresh-milk brands focused on low-temperature milk, and in 2026 the company was preparing a Hong Kong H-share listing. As president of New Hope's consumer investment platform Caogen Zhiben, he chairs Chengdu cold-chain logistics firm Xianshenghuo (Fresh-SCM). It was founded in 2016 and reportedly valued at RMB 10B after its 2022 Series B.
interesting_fact: New Hope Dairy deliberately chose fresh low-temperature milk to avoid Yili and Mengniu's strength in shelf-stable milk. Its flagship '24-hour' fresh milk is sold only on the day it ships, with no more than 24 hours on the shelf.
deep_cut_fact: He jokes that he is New Hope Group's 'dingzihu' (holdout): of the 20-plus university graduates who joined with him, he was the only one who stayed. He also says he had never worked in dairy and called himself a dairy 'outsider' when he took over New Hope Dairy in 2004.

public_contacts.value: nhdzqb@newhope.cn (New Hope Dairy board office / securities dept)

notes: Identity 'uncertain' only because the input calls him 'founder' of Fresh-SCM. Sources (36Kr) list Xi Gang (席刚) as chairman of Xianshenghuo/Fresh-SCM, which was incubated by New Hope's Caogen Zhiben, and its legal rep is Sun Xiaoyu. This is very likely the right person. Chairman role confirmed in New Hope Dairy's March 2026 board notice (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-03-12/1225005444.PDF). Relevant to a cold-chain/logistics angle.

name: David Leiberman
current_role: Co-founder of Triller, Mibblio and Console; co-founder of The Lorca (hospitality retreats, self-described). Current day-to-day role unclear.
profile: New York musician, teacher and app builder. He co-founded children's music-app maker Mibblio and then, with his cousin Sammy Rubin, Triller, the AI-powered music-video app (founded around 2015) that later attracted celebrity investors and a reported $1B+ valuation. He later co-founded Console, a Web3 Discord-style community platform, with Chris Castig.
interesting_fact: Triller started as a family project: he co-founded it with his cousin Sammy Rubin, after the two had built Mibblio, a music-making app for toddlers.
deep_cut_fact: Before Triller he helped create the Disney Frozen Karaoke app. He describes himself as a teacher and musician, and also co-founded The Lorca, a contemporary retreat in the Catskills plus a midcentury motel in the Adirondacks.
notes: No longer prominent at Triller. Avoid Triller's later corporate/financial troubles in outreach. Facts come mostly from his self-written Product Hunt profile. The Lorca's site appears to be thelorca.com, but I could not confirm his link to it independently.

name: Matt Robinson
current_role: Partner, Accel (London), investing in AI, inference, security and software; co-founder and board member of GoCardless
profile: Oxford graduate and ex-McKinsey consultant who co-founded London payments company GoCardless with Hiroki Takeuchi and Tom Blomfield, leading business, marketing and sales. He then founded and ran Nested, a proptech start-up that tackled the cash-buyer disadvantage in UK house sales. He joined Accel as an investor in 2024 and has angel-invested in Cleo, Gamma, n8n and Wayve.
interesting_fact: GoCardless was started by three Oxford students, Robinson, Hiroki Takeuchi and Tom Blomfield. Blomfield later founded Monzo, making the trio an unusually prolific UK fintech founding team.
deep_cut_fact: His Accel profile lists his favourite works as Jez Butterworth's play 'Jerusalem' and Tom Stoppard's 'Arcadia'.
notes: As an active VC focused on AI inference, he is a natural fit for a data-center themed podcast. Easiest to reach via Accel or X. He has said the early GoCardless team 'literally made every mistake you could' (https://smallbusiness.co.uk/gocardless-founder-matt-robinson-now-shaking-property-industry-2534362/).
